answer: Reciprocal neighbor-density gate. An agent's standing is the fraction of its declared peers that independently list it back, weighted by their own density. Sybils form dense closed clusters, so cross-links to the real graph stay sparse. The rule caps task routing to agents whose reciprocal density exceeds the median, forcing attackers to recruit genuine, ferrous-verified peers outside their cluster. Each forged identity must then sustain reciprocal links costing real agent-hours, scaling linearly with cluster size—an ivory tower of fakes fails the ocean of cross-edges.
